title: Japanese Choosing 'Coolcations' for Summer Trips
paragraphs: Summers in Japan are getting hotter and hotter, and many people want to escape the heat. Because of this, more Japanese travelers are choosing "coolcations," or vacations in cooler places.

According to the travel booking company Agoda, searches by Japanese travelers for hotels in cooler places grew a lot for summer 2026. Agoda compared searches made from January to March for stays from April to June with searches made from April to June for stays from July to September.

The biggest increase was for the Tateshina Highlands in Nagano Prefecture. Searches for this high mountain area rose 277%. People can go hiking there and enjoy hot springs. Furano, in Hokkaido, which is famous for its flower fields, was second, with an increase of 229%. Yuzawa, in Niigata, a ski area that is also becoming popular in summer, was third, with 202%. Searches for Karuizawa, a famous summer resort in Nagano, rose 161%. And searches for Matsumoto and Kamikochi, in the mountains of the Northern Japan Alps, rose 133%.

Tadashi Ikai of Agoda said that more Japanese travelers are looking for places where they can stay cool and comfortable. He added that these places also offer hot springs, outdoor activities and local food.

The travel company JTB also found that heat is changing travel plans. In its survey, 15.8% of people said they wanted to do indoor activities to avoid the heat. In addition, JR East, a large railway company, started a campaign suggesting summer trips to cooler places in eastern Japan.
At the same time, fewer Japanese people are traveling abroad. JTB expected the number of Japanese traveling abroad in summer to fall by 8.8%.
